description: The rules and guardrails that turn (level + template + arc + theme + personalization) into a safe, coherent, fresh book. This is the 'Adventure System' layer: story structure, pacing, emotional goals, variety, and the generation contract. It sits ON TOP of the reading engine and never overrides it — reading constraints always win.

story_guardrails.rule: The book must answer Who, What, Why, and How (see book-spec.four_questions). No 'things just happen' plots.
The child (from the profile) is the protagonist or co-protagonist and is present on most pages.

The child drives the resolution through effort, practice, kindness, cleverness, creativity, or teamwork. The problem is NOT solved by luck, coincidence, magic hand-wave, or an adult stepping in to fix it while the child watches.
Exactly one goal/problem per book. No subplots or second problems at early levels.
Stakes are mild and resolvable. No injury, illness, death, real danger, being lost-and-frightened, cruelty, bullying that isn't resolved kindly, or threatening villains.
The problem is actually resolved and the ending is warm and hopeful. Nothing is left hanging or bleak.
Any worry or sadness introduced must be relieved by the end. The child ends safe, capable, and okay.
Inclusive, respectful, stereotype-free portrayal of all people and roles.
The 'How' should follow from something set up earlier in the book (e.g., the red ball appears before it helps), not arrive from nowhere.
Convey the value through action, not a lecture. Avoid tacked-on morals ('Remember, always share!').
Focus on a single value or skill (the 'How') per book, so the emotional goal is clear.

objective_taxonomy.description: The book's core verb (book-spec.objective). One per book; a key variety axis.

pacing_by_level.description: How much story the reading level can carry. Page/sentence caps come from reading-levels.json; this maps them to story shape.

bands.notes: Barely-there conflict; the 'challenge' beat is a tiny wobble. Cozy/helping/discovery arcs fit best.
One clear problem, one or two attempts, warm win.
Dialogue and compound sentences allow more character voice.
Complex sentences (because/when) allow real cause-and-effect; feelings can be named.
Multi-step problems and a short paragraph per page; still one core goal.

variety.description: Guarantees no two books feel the same for a child, even at the same theme + level. The educational progression is identical; the experience is fresh.

anti_repeat_rules.rule: A child must never receive two books with an identical combination_key (all 5 axes the same).
Within the same theme + level, each new book must differ from each of the child's previous 3 books on at least 3 of the 5 axes.
Prefer changing 'objective' and 'setting' first — they most change the felt experience.

variety.per_child_memory: Store the combination_key of every book produced for a child; the selector reads it before choosing the next combination.

beat_guardrails.description: Generic do/don't for common beat roles, independent of template. The assembler distributes the level's page budget across beats by the template's weights.

do: establish the child and setting fast
dont: introduce the problem before the child

do: state one concrete want and why it matters
the child applies the value/skill (the How)

generation_contract.description: The structured process that produces one book. Reading constraints are enforced at every text step; story guardrails shape the content.
steps: 1. INPUTS: child profile, target level, theme.
2. SELECT (variety engine): choose template + arc + setting + tone_primary + objective, respecting anti_repeat_rules and the child's combination memory.
3. RESOLVE tokens: child name + allowed out-of-level theme/personal tokens (personalization.json caps).
4. FRAME four_questions: fill Who/What/Why/How; pick the value that will drive the How.
5. ASSEMBLE beats: distribute the level's page budget across the template beats (pacing_by_level).
6. GENERATE per page: write the child-decodable text within all reading constraints. (An optional adult read-aloud track exists in the schema but is PARKED/unused in current books.)

8. VALIDATE: run validation-rules (word eligibility, sentence length, practices_own_level, cumulative_review, story guardrails, safety). On hard fail, regenerate the flagged pages with tightened constraints.
9. ILLUSTRATE: per-page prompts threaded with the reference sheet.
10. RECORD: save combination_key to the child's memory for future variety.
self_check: Is every child-track word decodable-at-level, a live heart word, or an allowed token?
Does the CHILD solve it (effort/kindness/cleverness/practice/teamwork), not luck or an adult?
Is the 'How' set up earlier in the book?
One problem, resolved, with a warm ending and no lingering worry?
Does the book practice this level's new focus, not just review?
Is the combination_key sufficiently different from this child's recent books?
